canonical_claim: A pure unit may land with no consumer when it has exhaustive tests; this enables complex algorithms to arrive in independent reviewable pull requests.

topic: The work is sequenced as Phase 1
canonical_claim: The work is sequenced as Phase 1 A1–A4 crash/corruption fixes, Phase 2 A5–A10 correctness fixes, Phase 3 D1–D5 removals, Phase 4 C1–C4 and Ring-2 shrinking, Phase 5 B1–B4 performance/operability, and Phase 6 C5 plus E1–E3 and F1; C5 lands last.

topic: The 2-hour soak audit identified freshness-tag PUTs
canonical_claim: The 2-hour soak audit identified freshness-tag PUTs, HEAD probes, and physical-universe LIST enumeration as the main S3-cost levers; the reported AWS-standard synthetic cost was approximately $12.2 per 72 minutes, or about $10/hour.

canonical_claim: Round B targets a 40–50% reduction in read-class requests, a 25–30% reduction in PUT-class requests, and elimination of GC fold buffer churn, while leaving ref-protocol publishing, Ring-2 write buffers, and GC round cadence unchanged.

topic: Round B explicitly excludes shared write-path per-part-file
canonical_claim: Round B explicitly excludes shared write-path per-part-file buffer churn, adaptive GC round cadence, and rev.6 grace machinery, snapshot publication, lease reclaim, and seals.

canonical_claim: Round B sequencing is `§0` introspection first, then the full rev.6 plan, then §1 through §5 on the post-rev.6 baseline; the round avoids `CasStore` publish and lease code except for the `ProfileEvents.cpp` append points.

topic: The highest-ranked soak optimization lever was reducing
canonical_claim: The highest-ranked soak optimization lever was reducing per-file relink probes through manifest-hash identity.
If the approximately 2x NDJSON byte cost proves to be a bottleneck in soak, the only planned fallback is to re-binarize `cas_run` behind the same typed-open API; no fallback is pre-built.

The proposed stage-2 concurrent `commitPart` work was postponed because its upstream and generic-code impact was judged too strong and unpredictable; the research was retained in BACKLOG under `stage2-concurrent-commitpart-postponed`.

The fetch-handoff implementation order is pinning test, no-throw ledger install, poison and mint tightening, TLA mini-model, confirm core, B66b recursion brake, and then the test battery; if A1 is deferred, poison must be a hard fence.

The stage-1 implementation plan decomposes the work into 14 tasks: upload-pool wiring, event dispatch, detached upload, exception-safe merge, fan-out, memory cap, carve, caps, removal classification, chunked flush, decode bounds, payload removal, streaming recovery, and closure measurement.
S42 covers query-thread allocation faults only; thread-creation allocation faults are a separate class deferred to S43 because the ref append lane runs on the caller's thread.
After stage 1, stage 2's remaining cross-part target is serial `commitPart` dispatch, while CAS-only dedup HEAD and unconditional promote-manifest GET remain a separate roughly 12%-of-wall backlog.

The CAS merge-layout preparation is behaviour-preserving work to decompose complex algorithms, reseam tests, and produce review-sized pull requests; it does not land the feature or fix the cold-LIST and relink dangle-freedom gaps.
The target subsystem series lands in dependency order from `Primitives`/`Formats` through `Backend`, `Pool`, ref, writer, parts, GC, tools, and finally wiring; every unit PR changes no behaviour.
Splitting `cas_test_helpers.h` into per-layer fixtures is the highest-leverage test preparation and must precede splitting the largest CAS test files.
The preparation plan keeps the existing 3060-commit history and does not rewrite it; it creates a fresh branch from `altinity/antalya-26.6` and adds one unit and its tests per commit/PR.
Only the curated `docs/superpowers/cas/01`–`11` set is intended to ship as documentation; the broader `docs/superpowers/` worklogs, models, and reports do not ship.
Stage B completion is recorded only after T8 issues `STAGE B: PASS` or `FAIL` and T9 commits the mandatory closeout; T9 changes the verdict only if it proves a T8 measurement was wrong.
T6 depends on T1's pre-delete revalidation contract, T5 probe-A deletion, and T6a frontier attribution; T2 is not a T6 predecessor.
The destructive-enable dependency should join `Task 6` before `Task 7b`: the corrected critical path is `4d → 5 → (7 ∥ 5b) → 6 → 10f → 7a → 7b → 11`.
The public CAS roadmap is derived from verified `done`, user-visible `open`, known-limitations, and deliberately-rejected claims, while internal issue IDs are omitted from the public page.
Codecs-v3 integration order requires phase 2 before phase 4, permits phase 7 before or after phases 2 and 4, parks phase 3 until phase 2 is integrated and soaked, and reserves phase 8 for last.
The roadmap is a DONE/history roll-up; `BACKLOG.md` is the canonical list of still-pending CAS work, and the former root-shard-axis items are obsolete under the per-table snapshot+log model.
V1 should not add a disk cache, reuse `s3_cache`, public SQL introspection, distributed invalidation, generic path-result caching, or `MergeTree` changes.
The rollout order is API vocabulary and pure `PartFolderView`, no-retention facade, observability and guardrails, then bounded retained cache.

The architecture analysis recommends behavior-preserving refactor steps, including removing throwaway `CasDbg*` instrumentation, centralizing event emission and cursor keys, introducing `RefId`, `ObjectRef`, and `RoundContext`, and splitting `CasGc.cpp` only after preparatory reductions.
The consistency review recommends removing `CasDbg*` and `casDbgSampleHeadMiss`, or gating soak diagnostics behind a build flag or trace path instead of permanent `ProfileEvents`.

The first cache patch may introduce only `PartRefKey`, `Freshness`, `PartFolderView`, and pure manifest-tree query movement; retained capacity should remain zero or absent until the facade is observable and tested.
The cache rollout's no-retention facade phase has no one-`GET` performance promise; its acceptance target is behavior preservation with no normal bypass around the facade.
Retained-view enablement is the first rollout phase judged by the one-`GET` goal and must add request-count tests for repeated operations on an eligible part or projection folder.

The recommended codec cleanup order is comments and magic tables, enum and hash validation, RunFile record-bound checks, RunRef.checksum and payload_digest decisions, GcHeartbeat decision, binary version naming, and unused-placeholder removal

CAS codec proposal v2 assumes pre-release data with no dual-read compatibility scaffolding and one atomic cutover per format; CAS codec proposal v3 supersedes codecs_proposal_v2.md in full and treats the pre-release system as requiring one cutover per format with no dual-read compatibility scaffolding.
v2 migration order is shared framing, reframe Proto objects, move CAPT to Proto, update Streams, frame heartbeat and swap envelope guard, enable compression, then update docs and tooling
The v3 migration order is Formats bootstrap, control plane, refsnaplog, blob meta, runs, part manifest, blob envelope, and final provider-metadata and build-wiring cleanup
The T6b evidence led to the decision to remove `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` entirely, including its disabled value `0`, rather than retain the cap.

If a deadline cannot absorb the four Stage-B simplification tasks (no-reuse contract + retirement marker, removing NamespaceLifeId/incarnation plumbing, concentrating lifecycle decisions in CasRefCatalog, and the shortened removal sequence) plus the destructive-gate soak, the only defensible fallback is to ship with `UniversePolicy` still suppressing destructive GC rather than hurriedly landing the existing incarnation-based Task 5 and flipping Task 7b.

The CAS merge-layout preparation's R5 risk is calendar: roughly 20-25 PRs; the mitigation relies on the workstream parallelism plus keeping unit PRs small (200-600 lines) to keep review latency per PR low.

GCS generation binding's OAuth leg (`gcp_oauth` dialect with ADC credentials) is deliberately not implemented as a task because no ADC credentials exist on the validation stand; it is tracked only as a ROADMAP row, not gated on.
The introspection package is tracked under the `B15/B99/B169` release-readiness roadmap bullet for the mounts table, mount audit events, first gauges, and scoped/partial fsck.
The prod-scale scenario campaign was paused by the user after seven scenarios, with five formerly inconclusive priority verdicts resolved at prod scale.
Upstream-affecting fixes are intended for both upstream ClickHouse and `altinity/antalya-26.6`, while the CAS feature itself is intended for `altinity/antalya-26.6` only.

The upstream carve-out inventory includes `ReadBufferFromFileView` position corruption (B115), `ReadBufferFromS3` retry-cancel (B117), and `ThreadStatus` lifetime (B90) as standalone fixes with tests.

The `STAGE-A RETURN ITEM` marker currently appears in eight non-document files, and `tests/broken_tests.yaml` contains four related entries: `05008_ca_gc_snap_prune`, `04290_content_addressed_no_leftovers`, `05010_content_addressed_mounts_gc_health`, and `04295_content_addressed_mutation_no_leftovers`.

GCS generation binding intentionally does not auto-detect the endpoint, implement Compose-based conditional finalize for blobs above the single-PUT cap, add JSON or resumable uploads, or add requester-pays `x-goog-user-project` support.
The P3.1 design leaves beat cost and frequency tuning, structurally impossible in-degree recovery, GC liveness under contention, and first-open audit-event blindness out of scope.

Phase 1 excludes inline zero-byte log keys, `GC`-side fallback compaction, indexed or chunked multi-object snapshots, lazy snapshot blocks, per-round ref indexes, chunked namespace removal, and Keeper-based cross-epoch fencing.

The stabilization iteration defers the `CasGc.cpp` split, `Cas::Store` de-god-classing, generic `DiskSelector` per-disk isolation, `DiskObjectStorageTransaction` path virtualization, dead write-ordering code, and latent `MultipleDisksObjectStorageTransaction::shared_from_this` handling.
A new dedicated error code and MOVE-to-CA support are separate non-goals of the merge upload-retry fix; the former is only a documented escape hatch and the latter has its own design.
The F1-F11 design explicitly excludes F12, the relink kill-switch setting, and does not add compatibility aliases because CAS is pre-release with no persisted deployments.

The orphan-sweep fix direction is unresolved between emitting `-1` edges before deleting a manifest and refusing to sweep manifests whose edges may already have folded; neither should be implemented without the cost model.
B172 proposes moving blob staging to S3 with server-side copy to remove the local scratch-directory requirement and avoid rereading local files on condemned displacement.
The durable roster and `max_content_addressable_pool_format` setting are designed but deferred as pre-release schema-evolution machinery.
The remaining hot-pool snapshot byte-volume work is delta-runs plus periodic compaction, tracked as T1 and marked desirable.
The CAS-specific ephemeral reader pin for stateless or ref-less cross-node readers was only a design as of 2026-07-03 and is not implemented.
The chosen backup design still needs a pool-level volume object, a v1 decision on consolidated-only versus partial snapshot mirroring, daemon packaging, snapshot metadata format, and RBAC details.
The D1 plan makes rerunning the `CaBuildRootPrecommit` TLA+ model mandatory if `Build::precommitAdd` or `Build::promote` changes.
The D1 open risk is that if `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)` does not strictly increase on every recreate, implementation must use a sticky per-`server_root` incarnation allocator instead.

Native GCS Generation binding requires GOOG4 signing, precondition mapping from `If-None-Match: *` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0` and from `If-Match: <etag>` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: <generation>`, plus extraction from `x-goog-generation`; this was identified as a design implication but was not started in the initial probe run.
Azure validation was not started, and GCS production follow-ups remain desirable: Compose finalization for writes larger than 1 GiB, `gcp_oauth` validation, and generation-aware LIST discovery.

A synchronous writer-triggerable fold barrier that activates the precommit edge before revalidation is the ideal zero-reupload fix, but it is out of scope because no production writer↔GC fold API exists.

The obsolete design reserved Phase 2 for measured optimizations such as delta `RunFile` levels, leveled compaction, Bloom or fence-pointer metadata, adaptive handoff thresholds, and optional preflight or per-namespace restart; no Phase 1 authority or invariant may depend on them.

A complete fix for the non-Atomic `detached` ambiguity requires a caller-provided database/table structural anchor at metadata-storage entry points, plumbed through `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` into `PartPathParser` as a Phase-2 change.
`scenarios/README.md` and `s03_s05_scale.py` still contain `root_shards` text that contradicts the rewritten S08 oracle and should be corrected or folded into the standing documentation-refresh item.
A merge upload failure must retry the upload from the staged part rather than rerunning the whole merge.

Phase 3 converts `cas_ref_log` and `cas_ref_snap` to Always-compressed text, re-derives JSON-inflated byte budgets, preserves key-to-body `ns` and `txn_id` binding, and updates builders and parsers for the `.zst` suffix.
Phase 4 converts the fixed 22-byte `CasBlobMeta` sidecar to one-line JSON while keeping deduplication, resurrection, and token semantics unchanged.

Phase 5 converts `CasRunFile` to sorted NDJSON with a trailer and whole-file CityHash128 seal verification on every full read, while deleting the block/footer machinery and sequentially-unused seek APIs; the coupled `part_manifest_cleanup` fold-seal field removal depends on phase 2.

Phase 6 converts `CasManifestCodec` to a JSON descriptor followed by a `head -v` banner payload zone, verifies regenerated padding and banners, and follows phase 5 because `RunKind::ManifestEntries` and the embedded stream surface are shared.

Phase 7 converts `CasEnvelope` to a 256-byte JSON header line padded with spaces, keeps payload offset 256, removes `hash_algo`, `domain_id`, `header_hash`, and `writer_version`, and treats former TLV fields as `!`-critical keys.
Phase 8 is strictly last and covers the provider-metadata mirror, documentation finalization, and reducing or deleting `CasInspect`; protobuf build removal is already assigned to phase-2 Task 7.
Bulk write-replica warm-up was recorded as a future extension of build-owned pins, using a union of many manifest closures or a snapshot-window payload.

The generic AsyncLoader issue and upstream issue draft propose allowing `DETACH TABLE` for a table whose async load job is `FAILED` to reach existing state-erasing plumbing, or adding an explicit retry-on-touch/system re-trigger mechanism for failed table loads; the draft is for manual review and filing, not yet filed.
Adaptive tuning of the `head_first` deduplication threshold is deferred until a cold bulk-load benchmark quantifies the HEAD-plus-PUT cost.
Real GCS end-to-end coverage is deferred until GCS leaves experimental status because current CAS integration tests use RustFS and only test GCS request transformation at unit level.

The Stage B destructive-baseline report must measure sequential GC costs by phase and S3 verb, name untimed spans rather than estimate them, and rank falsifiable opportunities for a later `MultiDelete` or delete-concurrency round.

The remaining `stageATransition` migration is primarily a test-fixture migration: the audit found 295 source hits, with 291 in tests, one production declaration, and one production fallback use inside `resolveLifeOrSentinel`.

The ref side still lacks `NamespaceLifeId::fromLiveHandle`, a ref-side rebirth-alias reader test, and a ref-side zero-catalog-GET hot-read test; `CasRefLedger.cpp` still has ten `CasRefCatalog::read` sites in birth, reconcile, publish-admission, recovery, and janitor paths.

The `CaGcDestructiveGateCore` model does not cover the non-authoritative-universe posture, where production must suppress destruction regardless of the other physical-gate conjuncts; that posture is asserted by `CasGcFrontierGate.HiddenPlusOneInAnUnknownNamespaceIsRefusedByTheProductionDefault`.

The `stage5_lazytrim` positive safety claim under `EnableLazyTrim = TRUE` remains unproven by TLC after a four-hour `-workers 1` run, with `1,333,723,653` states generated, `233,198,128` distinct, and `24,395,446` queued.

The sharding arm remains unproven because `sab_crosssharddisplacement`, `sab_reducerownsfence`, and `stage5_sharding` all hit the model error `UnchangedCompositeVars`; consequently `EnableSharding`'s cross-shard displacement and reducer-owns-fence guards were not exercised by TLC.
Replacing the honest `RemintEpoch` literal `1` with `epochCeiling + 1` is an unimplemented candidate refinement that would avoid historical fenced-epoch collisions.

The `CaCasMountCore` recovery-generation gate does not model the `_ckpt` CAS itself or prove that `slot-occupy`, `_ckpt`, and install present the same rechecked generation; that remains a plan obligation.
The catalog-token half of zombie-install prevention remains owned by `CaRefCatalogCore`; the mount model proves only the generation credential and the install must present both credentials.
Release readiness still requires capability gate B31, real-S3 GC validation, a backup/restore runbook, `SYSTEM` control commands B197, RustFS integration tests B125, and repository hygiene B131.

The post-codecs campaign queue lists `#36` S36 MOVE PART/PARTITION scenarios, `#37` merge upload-retry investigation, `#38` production-scale scenarios 01–36, and `#40` CAS unit-test ASan compatibility including TSan verification of the rev.6 F3-1a race.
Incremental point-updatable in-degree remains open as Phase 4 Lever B; it is intended to make a non-idle small-delta GC round O(delta).

The first production release still requires Azure real-S3 GC validation, a 4-hour-or-longer chaos soak on a compacting store, and the `B207` fsck race fix as release gates; AWS and GCS validation are recorded as done.

The remaining production-release operability gates include `B197` SYSTEM control commands, `B13` migration and mixed-version rollout rules, `B180` pool-format version breadcrumb, `B192` event-name review, `B198` backup/restore runbook, `B48`/`B167a/f` clean shutdown, `B196` S3 permit capping, and `B131` repository hygiene.

The testing roadmap leaves 4-hour continuous chaos, S12 10-replica shared-pool testing, S22 throttling/retry testing, S27 LIST-pagination ambiguity testing, D3 full-round `gc_shards > 1` tests, and B5 per-server-tree integration reconciliation as open work.

Generic fixes for `ThreadStatus` B90, `ReadBufferFromFileView` B115, `ReadBufferFromS3` B117, `LocalObjectStorage` TOCTOU, the `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog` null-writer guard, `copyS3File` message formatting, `Expect: 100-continue`, `S3Exception::isPreconditionFailed()`, and the GCS dialect/signer should be carved into separate upstream pull requests to reduce the fork's Ring-2 diff.

The independently reviewable upstream split should cover GCS conditional-write support, the `renameParts` disk-transaction-close durability fix, `ReadBufferFromFileView` B115 with its gtest battery, S3 412 no-retry with `isPreconditionFailedError`, and the core CAS backend.

The `LocalObjectStorage::listObjects` NUL-byte guard, the redundant `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkAlterPartitionIsPossible` override, the B90 parent-retain fix, the B37 dedup-log fail-closed change, and concurrent-listing snapshot semantics are candidates for independent upstream contributions or cleanup.

Once `precommit` publishes the empty covering part before the `data_parts` lock, the hand-placed `commitTransaction()` in `MergeTreeData::removePartsInRangeFromWorkingSet` should be removed as redundant.

After the two-phase contract, `DataPartStorageOnDiskBase::freeze`, `MergeTreeData::restorePartFromBackup`, and B58 projection commit sites should use the `precommit`/`commit` pair and express the shared-transaction rule once.

The redundant `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkAlterPartitionIsPossible` override can be deleted independently of `[TXN-ONE-PIPELINE]`, and B37, B90, and `LocalObjectStorage` robustness fixes can be extracted as standalone upstream contributions.

As of the architecture doc: probe logic for backend conditional-delete conformance is DONE; GCS generation binding is TODO; versioned mode (token = versionId) is a future, explicitly separate feature.

The CAS merge-layout preparation left open decision D1 (granularity) unresolved: the proposal is fine-grained, one complex algorithm per PR (about 20-25 PRs) relying on workstream parallelism, versus the alternative of eight medium PRs of about 5-6k lines each.

The CAS merge-layout preparation left open decision D2 (sequencing of workstream B) unresolved: the proposal is to complete all of workstreams B and C before carving, versus the alternative of carving each hot spot as soon as it is extracted, which gets reviewer feedback earlier but keeps the working branch alive longer and risks divergence.
